messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-severity: multiple GPU hosts in us-west1 showing NVLINK link error spikes and host-initiated device resets. Pager -> @alex (oncall).
alex (oncall): on it, paging the team. any customer-facing impact yet?
sam (support): saw 503s from some inference routes ~04:12-04:18 UTC, about 6 customers hit intermittently, nothing persistent. I have the request ids.
maria (sre): looking at cluster metrics, GPU kernel logs show repeated nvlink_timeout and driver_reset events on host gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-19. Rolling counts spiked at 04:10 UTC. attaching tail of dmesg.
jon (eng-runtime): can you paste the kernel lines? nvlink stuff can be noisy but we need to know if it's causing OOMs.
maria (sre): ```
[04:09:53] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: nvlink: link flapping detected, status 0x304
[04:10:01] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: nvlink: timeout waiting for peer response
[04:10:04] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: driver: Resetting GPU due to error
[04:10:05] kernel: device-mapper: zombie process handling GPU reset
[04:11:30] nvme0n1: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 0
```
alex (oncall): thanks. priya, any host-level events from cloud side? maintenance? noisy neighbor?
priya (cloud-ops): no scheduled maint. Cloud reported an underlying host firmware auto-recovery at 04:10 for the physical machine hosting gpu-node-12; they noted a PCIe link retrain. Not identical terminology but likely related. Opening a ticket with provider, but need immediate mitigations.
jon (eng-runtime): runtime impact: these nodes host batch and some realtime. Our routing policy should fallback to warm pool, but looks like some long running sessions hit a reset and returned 503. Can we cordon the two hosts and evacuate?
maria (sre): I can cordon + drain via kube: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will start now.
alex (oncall): do it. mark as mitigating. also enable canary fallback to model-small variant for affected customers to mitigate tail latency.
sam (support): posting incident banner to status page: "Investigating GPU host instability causing intermittent errors for inference routes in us-west1. Mitigation in progress."
jon (eng-runtime): while draining, can we reduce batch sizes / KV cache TTL on the affected routes to reduce requeue? change pushed to routing service: `--batch-size=32 -> 16` for route /v1/generate, live now.
maria (sre): drain completed for gpu-node-12 at 04:22 UTC, pods rescheduled to healthy nodes; kernel logs show one more reset on gpu-node-19 at 04:26, cordoning that next.
priya (cloud-ops): provider ticket: case #PR-8921 — they observed a firmware micro-reset on NIC and suggested host firmware patch, ETA for remediation window 6 hours. They also flagged potential noisy neighbor PCIe retrains.
alex (oncall): hypothesis list: 1) NVLINK hardware link degradation causing driver resets. 2) Host firmware bug triggered by noisy neighbor IO pattern -> PCIe retrain causing nvlink timeouts. 3) Model memory pressure causing driver OOM -> driver->reset chain (less likely given kernel lines). Anyone disagree or add?
jon (eng-runtime): add 4) power/thermal transients causing link flaps (we saw thermal spikes on one host earlier this week).
maria (sre): tracking evidence: attaching timeline below and note flags we want to gather: `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,POWER,DIAGS` dumps, full dmesg, syslog, instance host logs, provider's host event log.
--- TIMELINE ---
04:07 UTC - small uptick in inference 95th pct latency on route prod-realtime
04:09 UTC - nvlink link flaps start on gpu-node-12
04:10 UTC - driver reset and host firmware auto-recovery reported by provider
04:11-04:18 UTC - customer 503s observed by support (sam)
04:22 UTC - cordon+drain gpu-node-12, traffic ramped to other nodes
04:26 UTC - reset observed on gpu-node-19, cordon in progress
04:35 UTC - routing fallback to model-small live for some customers
-----------------
alex (oncall): good. Maria, capture the nvlink diag dumps and attach to incident. Jon, can you run a repro job hitting high NVLINK transfers to see if we can reproduce locally in our staging with same driver/firmware? Use the same model and batch profile.
jon (eng-runtime): starting stress repro on staging now, will record PCIe/NVLink counters. Will also try with updated driver we have in canary to see if that avoids reset.
sam (support): updated status page: mitigation in place, customers on small model, monitoring. I'll flag impacted billing windows and notify account teams for those 6 customers.
priya (cloud-ops): suggestion for temporary mitigation: enable anti-affinity for GPU pods to reduce collocated heavy IO patterns until provider rolls firmware. We can push a node-pool label and reschedule. Would add cost but reduce noisy-neighbor risk.
maria (sre): agreed. implementing anti-affinity for high-IO jobs now for us-west1. Changing pod spec with `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` and `podAntiAffinity` to avoid colocations.
alex (oncall): handoff plan: I'm oncall until 06:00 UTC. If provider ETA not updated and more resets occur, escalate to infra oncall and product. Next oncall @jon will take over after 06:00. Please post final notes and evidence in this thread for RCA.
jon (eng-runtime): repro started; initial run shows elevated nvlink CRC errors after sustained transfer; switching driver to our canary build suppressed the resets for now. collecting logs and diff.
maria (sre): exported `dmesg` + `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots and uploaded to incident ticket PR-8921 and our internal incident storage. link: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1854762020
sam (support): customers notified via account teams; no escalations yet.
alex (oncall): marking incident state: mitigated (traffic rerouted + nodes drained + anti-affinity applied). severity will remain 2 until provider confirms firmware/host fix. Next steps: aggregate logs, reproduce in staging, coordinate provider firmware remediation, postmortem template assigned to jon for RCA draft.
jon (eng-runtime): will own RCA draft; will include repro steps, kernel/nvlink counters, and compare driver canary vs prod. target initial RCA by EOD.
maria (sre): adding follow-up action to run fleet-wide health check for NVLINK/PCIe errors and schedule preventive drains for nodes hitting >X resets in 24h.
alex (oncall): thanks all. closing active paging. everyone please add any missed notes to this thread before handoff. :white_check_mark:
